ROC Curves

Dylan Maddux

2025-04-22

Logistic Model

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(pROC)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 16))

crab <- read.table("http://www.stat.ufl.edu/~aa/cat/data/Crabs.dat", 
                   header = TRUE)

## Make vector of factor
crab$colorf <- factor(crab$color)

fit <- glm(y ~ width, family = binomial, data = crab)
summary(fit)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = y ~ width, family = binomial, data = crab)
## 
## Deviance Residuals: 
##     Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max  
## -2.0281  -1.0458   0.5480   0.9066   1.6942  
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept) -12.3508     2.6287  -4.698 2.62e-06 ***
## width         0.4972     0.1017   4.887 1.02e-06 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 225.76  on 172  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 194.45  on 171  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 198.45
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4
exp(coef(fit))
##  (Intercept)        width 
## 4.326214e-06 1.644162e+00

Confusion Matrix / Classification Table

## Make vector of factor
crab$colorf <- factor(crab$color)

fit <- glm(y ~ width + colorf, family = binomial, data = crab)

## Sample proportion crabs with sat
(prop <- sum(crab$y) / nrow(crab))
## [1] 0.6416185
predval <- as.numeric(fitted(fit) > prop)

xtabs(~ crab$y + predval)
##       predval
## crab$y  0  1
##      0 43 19
##      1 36 75
## Try again with pi0 = 50
predval50 <- as.numeric(fitted(fit) > 0.5)
xtabs(~ crab$y + predval50)
##       predval50
## crab$y  0  1
##      0 31 31
##      1 15 96
table(crab$y, predval50)
##    predval50
##      0  1
##   0 31 31
##   1 15 96

ROC

rocplot <- roc(y ~ fitted(fit), data = crab)

with(rocplot, cbind(thresholds, specificities, sensitivities)) %>% head()
##      thresholds specificities sensitivities
## [1,]       -Inf    0.00000000      1.000000
## [2,] 0.07687681    0.01612903      1.000000
## [3,] 0.12358898    0.01612903      0.990991
## [4,] 0.14914129    0.03225806      0.990991
## [5,] 0.15834386    0.04838710      0.990991
## [6,] 0.18820139    0.08064516      0.990991
with(rocplot, cbind(thresholds, specificities, sensitivities)) %>% tail()
##        thresholds specificities sensitivities
## [104,]  0.9429514             1   0.045045045
## [105,]  0.9484416             1   0.036036036
## [106,]  0.9610099             1   0.027027027
## [107,]  0.9725402             1   0.018018018
## [108,]  0.9806093             1   0.009009009
## [109,]        Inf             1   0.000000000
plot.roc(rocplot, legacy.axes = TRUE)

auc(rocplot)
## Area under the curve: 0.7714
library(plotROC)

## Put fitted values back in data.frame
crab$fitval <- fitted(fit)

ggplot(crab) + geom_roc(aes(d = y, m = fitval))

ggplot(crab, aes(color = colorf)) + geom_roc(aes(d = y, m = fitval)) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1")

m1 <- ggplot(crab) + geom_roc(aes(d = y, m = fitval))
m2 <- ggplot(crab, aes(color = colorf)) + geom_roc(aes(d = y, m = fitval))

calc_auc(m1)
##   PANEL group       AUC
## 1     1    -1 0.7713601
calc_auc(m2) # AUC for each level of factor
##   PANEL group colorf       AUC
## 1     1     1      1 0.5185185
## 2     1     2      2 0.7101449
## 3     1     3      3 0.8365385
## 4     1     4      4 0.5904762

Exercises

# read in data
gsw <- read.csv("https://remiller1450.github.io/data/GSWarriors.csv")
gsw$win_binary <- ifelse(gsw$Win == "W", 1, 0) # response var

Part A Fit a logistic regression model using only FG3A as a predictor. This variable represents the number of three-point shots attempted in a game. Interpret the fitted coefficient.

mod1 <- glm(win_binary~FG3A, family = "binomial", data = gsw)
summary(mod1)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = win_binary ~ FG3A, family = "binomial", data = gsw)
## 
## Deviance Residuals: 
##     Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max  
## -2.2709   0.4331   0.4717   0.4992   0.5947  
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
## (Intercept)  1.02624    1.90428   0.539    0.590
## FG3A         0.03426    0.06098   0.562    0.574
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 56.745  on 81  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 56.423  on 80  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 60.423
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 5

The odds of winning increase by exp(0.03426) = 1.03 for each additional three-point shot attempted in a game.

Part B Fit a logistic model again, this time using both FG3A (attempts) and FG3 where FG3 represents the number of attempts actually made. Examine the coefficients and explain why the sign of FG3A has changed.

mod2 <- glm(win_binary~FG3A+FG3, family = "binomial", data = gsw)
summary(mod2)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = win_binary ~ FG3A + FG3, family = "binomial", data = gsw)
## 
## Deviance Residuals: 
##     Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max  
## -2.8037   0.2071   0.3411   0.5289   1.2065  
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)   
## (Intercept)  0.93957    2.02162   0.465  0.64210   
## FG3A        -0.10074    0.07754  -1.299  0.19386   
## FG3          0.36516    0.13951   2.617  0.00886 **
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 56.745  on 81  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 48.043  on 79  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 54.043
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 6

The sign of FG3A has changed in this model because when considering three-point shots made, additional three-point attempts wouldn’t increase the odds of winning beyond what is accounted for with the successful three point attempts.

Part C Create ROC curves associated with each of the models created.

library(plotROC)
library(ggplot2)

gsw$fit <- fitted(mod1)
ggplot(gsw) + geom_roc(aes(d = win_binary, m = fit))

gsw$fit <- fitted(mod2)
ggplot(gsw) + geom_roc(aes(d = win_binary, m = fit))
